name: Auto-Remediation
summary: AI agent that fixes findings from a scan, validates the fix branch (build + re-scan), and opens one pull request with per-issue commits. Phase 1 keeps partial fixes and always opens the PR with a status summary.
description: AI agent that fixes findings from a scan, validates the fix branch (build + re-scan), and opens one pull request with per-issue commits. Phase 1 keeps partial fixes and always opens the PR with a status summary.
pipelineYaml:
pipeline:
  name: Auto-Remediation Sample
  identifier: remediationAgentSample
  projectIdentifier: "{{projectId}}"
  orgIdentifier: "{{orgId}}"
  tags:
    agents-library: generated
  properties:
    ci:
      codebase:
        repoName: <+input>
        build: <+input>
  stages:
    - stage:
        name: Run Auto-Remediation
        identifier: Run_remediationAgent
        type: CI
        spec:
          cloneCodebase: true
          platform:
            os: Linux
            arch: Amd64
          runtime:
            type: Cloud
            spec: {}
          execution:
            steps:
              - step:
                  type: Agent
                  name: Auto-Remediation
                  identifier: remediationAgent
                  spec:
                    agentName: remediationAgent
                    agentSettings:
                      execution_id: <+pipeline.executionId>
                      account_id: <+account.identifier>
                      org_id: <+org.identifier>
                      project_id: <+project.identifier>
                      llm_connector: <+input>
                      scm_connector: <+input>
agentYaml:
template:
  inputs:
    execution_id:
      type: string
      label: AI Workflow Execution ID
      required: true
      default: <+pipeline.executionId>
      ui:
        tooltip: Enter the AI Workflow execution ID for this remediation run. Auto-populated by Harness at trigger time; override only for replay or debugging.
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    account_id:
      type: string
      label: Account ID
      required: true
      default: <+account.identifier>
      ui:
        tooltip: Enter the Harness account ID that owns this remediation run. Auto-populated at trigger time; override only for replay or debugging.
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    org_id:
      type: string
      label: Org ID
      required: true
      default: <+org.identifier>
      ui:
        tooltip: Enter the Harness organization ID that owns this remediation run. Auto-populated at trigger time; override only for replay or debugging.
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    project_id:
      type: string
      label: Project ID
      required: true
      default: <+project.identifier>
      ui:
        tooltip: Enter the Harness project ID that owns this remediation run. Auto-populated at trigger time; override only for replay or debugging.
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    scan_id:
      type: string
      label: Scan ID (scan-completion only)
      default: ""
      ui:
        tooltip: Enter the scan ID whose findings should be remediated. Auto-populated when triggered by a scan-completion event; leave empty for future scheduled or on-demand runs. Must be set together with Target ID.
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    target_id:
      type: string
      label: Target ID
      default: ""
      ui:
        tooltip: Enter the target ID being remediated. Auto-populated on a scan-completion trigger; must be set together with Scan ID.
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    target_name:
      type: string
      label: Target / Repository Name
      default: ""
      ui:
        tooltip: Enter the target display name, in owner/repo form when available. Auto-populated from the scan-completion event.
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    repo_url:
      type: string
      label: Repository Clone URL
      default: ""
      ui:
        tooltip: Enter the Git remote URL from the originating scan, used when the stage clone of the codebase does not resolve the repository. Auto-populated from the scan target URL.
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    target_variant_name:
      type: string
      label: Target Variant Name
      default: ""
      ui:
        tooltip: Enter the target variant name from the originating scan. Used as the pull request target branch when present; auto-populated from the scan-completion event.
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    source_branch:
      type: string
      label: Source Branch
      default: ""
      ui:
        tooltip: Enter the branch the originating scan ran on. Used as the fix pull request base branch and to clone the repository; auto-populated from the scan-completion event Git metadata.
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    scm_provider:
      type: string
      label: SCM Provider
      default: ""
      ui:
        tooltip: Enter the source control provider of the repository, such as github, gitlab, bitbucket, or harness_code. Selects the pull request creation path; auto-populated from the scan-completion event.
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    scan_types:
      type: string
      label: Issue Types to Remediate
      default: ""
      ui:
        tooltip: "Specify a comma-separated list of issue types to remediate. Leave empty to remediate all supported types. Stamped from the AI Workflow configuration."
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    severity_types:
      type: string
      label: Severities to Remediate
      default: "CRITICAL,HIGH"
      ui:
        tooltip: "Specify a comma-separated list of severities to remediate, from CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, and INFO. Leave empty to remediate every severity."
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    only_true_positive_issue_types:
      type: string
      label: Only True-Positive Issue Types
      default: ""
      ui:
        tooltip: "Specify a comma-separated list of issue types that require a TRUE_POSITIVE triage verdict before a fix is attempted. Each type is filtered independently. Leave empty to apply no triage filter. When set, triage must cover those types and this run stays queued until triage reaches a terminal state."
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    exclude_unreachable:
      type: boolean
      label: Exclude Unreachable Issues
      default: false
      ui:
        tooltip: "Enable to skip issues that are not reachable, matching the Exclude issues that are not reachable filter. Applies only where reachability data is present on the occurrences."
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    exclude_repo_patterns:
      type: string
      label: Exclude Repositories
      default: ""
      ui:
        tooltip: "Specify comma-separated glob patterns that exclude repositories from remediation, for example \"*-test,dev-*\"."
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    llm_connector:
      type: connector
      label: LLM Connector
      required: true
      ui:
        connectorCategories:
          - AI
        tooltip: Select the large language model connector used to generate fixes. Sub-agents require an Anthropic (Claude) backend today.
        placeholder: Select LLM Connector
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    scm_connector:
      type: connector
      label: SCM Connector
      required: true
      oneof:
        - Github
        - Gitlab
        - Bitbucket
        - AzureRepo
        - Git
      ui:
        tooltip: "Select the source control connector for the repository being remediated. It both clones the codebase into the stage and pushes the fix branch to open the pull request, so its credential must allow pushes and pull request creation. For GitHub, use HTTP authentication with a personal access token that holds the classic repo scope; for Harness Code, use a Git connector with a personal access token. Stamped from the AI Workflow configuration and required because this agent runs outside the project where the repository lives."
        placeholder: Select SCM Connector
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    mcp_connectors:
      type: array
      label: MCP Connectors
      default: []
      ui:
        component: array
        input:
          inputType: connector
          inputConfig:
            connectorTypes:
              - Mcp
        tooltip: Select the Model Context Protocol connectors the agent mounts for Harness pipeline execution, failure diagnosis, and finding reads.
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    harness_base_url:
      type: string
      label: Harness Base URL
      default: ""
      ui:
        tooltip: "Enter the Harness API gateway base URL used by the first-party harness Model Context Protocol server and its REST fallback, for example https://app.harness.io. Pairs with the account secret harness_api_key; leave empty to use the agent runtime default."
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    validation_mode:
      type: string
      label: Validation Mode
      default: agent_validated
      options:
        - agent_validated
        - deferred
      ui:
        component: select
        tooltip: "Select how a fix branch is verified before the pull request opens. Choose agent_validated to run the configured validation pipelines, scanning first when a scan pipeline is set and building after that scan succeeds, or deferred to skip validation and rely on your own pull request checks. A run behaves as deferred when neither pipeline is configured."
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    scan_pipeline_id:
      type: string
      label: Scan Pipeline
      default: ""
      ui:
        tooltip: "Enter the identifier of a scan-only pipeline that re-scans the fix branch to confirm findings are remediated, which is checked before the build pipeline. It must use the same scanner as the originating scan, clone the target repository, and expose the codebase branch as a runtime input. Leave empty to skip the scan check and run build-only or deferred validation."
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    scan_pipeline_org:
      type: string
      label: Scan Pipeline Org
      default: ""
      ui:
        tooltip: Enter the Harness organization that holds the scan pipeline, which may differ from the organization running the remediation. Leave empty to use this remediation run's organization.
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    scan_pipeline_project:
      type: string
      label: Scan Pipeline Project
      default: ""
      ui:
        tooltip: Enter the Harness project that holds the scan pipeline. Leave empty to use this remediation run's project.
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    scan_input_set:
      type: string
      label: Scan Pipeline Input Set
      default: ""
      ui:
        tooltip: Enter the input set identifier that supplies the scan pipeline's required runtime inputs. The fix branch is passed automatically as the codebase branch.
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    build_pipeline_id:
      type: string
      label: Build Pipeline
      default: ""
      ui:
        tooltip: "Enter the identifier of a build-only pipeline that confirms the fix branch still builds. It runs after the scan pipeline reaches a successful terminal state, or immediately when no scan pipeline is set, and runs even when findings remain. It must clone the target repository and expose the codebase branch as a runtime input; leave empty to skip the build check."
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    build_pipeline_org:
      type: string
      label: Build Pipeline Org
      default: ""
      ui:
        tooltip: Enter the Harness organization that holds the build pipeline. Leave empty to use this remediation run's organization.
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    build_pipeline_project:
      type: string
      label: Build Pipeline Project
      default: ""
      ui:
        tooltip: Enter the Harness project that holds the build pipeline. Leave empty to use this remediation run's project.
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    build_input_set:
      type: string
      label: Build Pipeline Input Set
      default: ""
      ui:
        tooltip: Enter the input set identifier that supplies the build pipeline's required runtime inputs. The fix branch is passed automatically as the codebase branch.
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    max_fix_attempts:
      type: number
      label: Max Fix Attempts
      default: 4
      ui:
        tooltip: "Limit how many fix and validate iterations the joint scan and build loop performs, where one attempt is a single validation round of the scan pipeline followed by the build pipeline when both are configured. For example, 2 fixes every issue and validates, re-fixes once if the joint gate is not green, and then opens the pull request with whatever remains. The same budget covers scan and build re-fixes."
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    remediation_time_budget_seconds:
      type: number
      label: Time Budget (seconds)
      default: 0
      ui:
        tooltip: "Set a soft wall-clock budget in seconds that caps only the start of new validation attempts, where 0 means unlimited. It never interrupts a pipeline wait already in progress and never gates fixing. When the elapsed time exceeds the budget before a new validation attempt, the agent pushes the fixes it completed, marks the rest unverified, and opens the pull request."
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    max_occurrences:
      type: number
      label: Max Occurrences Per Run
      default: 500
      ui:
        tooltip: "Limit how many finding occurrences a single run remediates so the working set stays bounded. Enter a value of 1 or greater."
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    additional_instructions:
      type: string
      label: Additional Instructions
      default: ""
      ui:
        component: textarea
        tooltip: Enter optional free-form guidance appended to the orchestrator prompt. Use it sparingly and prefer adjusting the filters above.
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    jira_enabled:
      type: boolean
      label: Jira Enabled
      default: false
      ui:
        tooltip: "Enable to create a summary Jira ticket once results are persisted. Auto-populated from the AI Workflow configuration on trigger, so leave it unchanged for automatic runs."
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    triggering_pipeline_id:
      type: string
      label: Triggering Pipeline ID
      default: ""
      ui:
        tooltip: Enter the identifier of the pipeline that produced the originating scan. Auto-populated on a scan-completion trigger and used for the pull request's originating scan link.
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    triggering_pipeline_execution_id:
      type: string
      label: Triggering Pipeline Execution ID
      default: ""
      ui:
        tooltip: Enter the execution ID of the originating scan pipeline. Auto-populated on a scan-completion trigger and used for the pull request's originating scan link.
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
    triggering_pipeline_build_number:
      type: string
      label: Triggering Pipeline Build Number
      default: ""
      ui:
        tooltip: "Enter the build or sequence number of the originating scan pipeline. Auto-populated on a scan-completion trigger and used in the fix branch name."
        allowedValueTypes:
          - fixed
          - runtime
          - expression
  layout:
    - scan_types
    - severity_types
    - only_true_positive_issue_types
    - exclude_unreachable
    - llm_connector
    - scm_connector
    - validation_mode
    - scan_pipeline_id
    - scan_pipeline_org
    - scan_pipeline_project
    - scan_input_set
    - build_pipeline_id
    - build_pipeline_org
    - build_pipeline_project
    - build_input_set
    - variant: more
      items:
        - max_fix_attempts
        - remediation_time_budget_seconds
        - exclude_repo_patterns
        - mcp_connectors
        - harness_base_url
        - max_occurrences
        - additional_instructions
        - triggering_pipeline_id
        - triggering_pipeline_execution_id
        - triggering_pipeline_build_number
        - execution_id
        - account_id
        - org_id
        - project_id
        - scan_id
        - target_id
        - target_name
        - target_variant_name
        - source_branch
        - scm_provider
        - repo_url
        - jira_enabled

  id: remediationAgent
  name: Auto-Remediation
  description: AI agent that fixes findings from a scan, validates the fix branch (build + re-scan), and opens one pull request with per-issue commits. Phase 1 keeps partial fixes and always opens the PR with a status summary.
  version: 1
  author: harness
  agent:
    group:
      steps:
        - name: Scope
          id: scope
          if: <+Always>
          run:
            container:
              image: harness/remediation-pre-plugin:latest
              connector: account.harnessImage
              pull_policy: always
            env:
              EXECUTION_ID: ${{inputs.execution_id}}
              ACCOUNT_ID: ${{inputs.account_id}}
              ORG_ID: ${{inputs.org_id}}
              PROJECT_ID: ${{inputs.project_id}}
              SCAN_ID: ${{inputs.scan_id}}
              TARGET_ID: ${{inputs.target_id}}
              TARGET_NAME: ${{inputs.target_name}}
              REPO_URL: ${{inputs.repo_url}}
              TARGET_VARIANT_NAME: ${{inputs.target_variant_name}}
              SOURCE_BRANCH: ${{inputs.source_branch}}
              SCM_PROVIDER: ${{inputs.scm_provider}}
              ISSUE_TYPES: ${{inputs.scan_types}}
              SEVERITY_TYPES: ${{inputs.severity_types}}
              ONLY_TRUE_POSITIVE_ISSUE_TYPES: ${{inputs.only_true_positive_issue_types}}
              EXCLUDE_UNREACHABLE: ${{inputs.exclude_unreachable}}
              EXCLUDE_REPO_PATTERNS: ${{inputs.exclude_repo_patterns}}
              MAX_OCCURRENCES: ${{inputs.max_occurrences}}
              VALIDATION_MODE: ${{inputs.validation_mode}}
              SCAN_PIPELINE_ID: ${{inputs.scan_pipeline_id}}
              SCAN_PIPELINE_ORG: ${{inputs.scan_pipeline_org}}
              SCAN_PIPELINE_PROJECT: ${{inputs.scan_pipeline_project}}
              SCAN_INPUT_SET: ${{inputs.scan_input_set}}
              BUILD_PIPELINE_ID: ${{inputs.build_pipeline_id}}
              BUILD_PIPELINE_ORG: ${{inputs.build_pipeline_org}}
              BUILD_PIPELINE_PROJECT: ${{inputs.build_pipeline_project}}
              BUILD_INPUT_SET: ${{inputs.build_input_set}}
              ORIGIN_EXECUTION_ID: <+pipeline.executionId>
              TRIGGERING_PIPELINE_ID: ${{inputs.triggering_pipeline_id}}
              TRIGGERING_PIPELINE_EXECUTION_ID: ${{inputs.triggering_pipeline_execution_id}}
              TRIGGERING_PIPELINE_BUILD_NUMBER: ${{inputs.triggering_pipeline_build_number}}
              SCOPE_FILE: /harness/sast_rem_scope.json
              AGENT_BUNDLE_DIR: /harness/output
              ADDITIONAL_INSTRUCTIONS: ${{inputs.additional_instructions}}
              MAX_FIX_ATTEMPTS: ${{inputs.max_fix_attempts}}
              PROMPT_VERSION: rem-v17
              HARNESS_STO_SERVICE_TOKEN: <+sto.serviceToken>
              HARNESS_STO_SERVICE_ENDPOINT: <+sto.serviceEndpoint>

        - name: print agent bundle
          id: printAgentBundle
          if: <+steps.scope.output.outputVariables.outcome> != "ZERO_IN_SCOPE"
          run:
            container:
              image: harness/remediation-pre-plugin:latest
              connector: account.harnessImage
            shell: Sh
            script: |-
              set -eu
              BUNDLE="${AGENT_BUNDLE_DIR:-/harness/output}"
              echo "──── agent bundle inventory: $BUNDLE ────"
              for req in task.txt skill/SKILL.md skill/subagents.json; do
                if [ ! -f "$BUNDLE/$req" ]; then
                  echo "ERROR: missing required $BUNDLE/$req"
                  exit 1
                fi
              done
              find "$BUNDLE" -type f 2>/dev/null | sort | while IFS= read -r f; do
                sz=$(wc -c < "$f" | tr -d ' ')
                printf '%8s  %s\n' "$sz" "$f"
              done
              echo "──── task.txt (FIX_BRANCH redacted) ────"
              sed -E 's/(FIX_BRANCH=).*/\1<redacted>/' "$BUNDLE/task.txt"
              echo "──── skill/subagents.json (full) ────"
              cat "$BUNDLE/skill/subagents.json"
              echo "──── skill/SKILL.md outline ────"
              echo "lines=$(wc -l < "$BUNDLE/skill/SKILL.md" | tr -d ' ')"
              grep -E '^#{1,3} ' "$BUNDLE/skill/SKILL.md" || true
              echo "──── skill/SKILL.md head (120 lines) ────"
              head -n 120 "$BUNDLE/skill/SKILL.md"
              echo "──── skill/SKILL.md Validation diagnosis § (if present) ────"
              awk '/^## Validation diagnosis/{p=1} p && /^## / && !/^## Validation diagnosis/{exit} p{print}' \
                "$BUNDLE/skill/SKILL.md" || true
            env:
              AGENT_BUNDLE_DIR: /harness/output

        - name: Remediate
          id: remediate
          if: <+steps.scope.output.outputVariables.outcome> != "ZERO_IN_SCOPE"
          on-failure:
            errors: all
            action: ignore
          run:
            container:
              image: harness/harness-ai-agent:0.1.77
              connector: account.harnessImage
              memory: "8Gi"
              cpu: "4"
            env:
              PLUGIN_HARNESS_CONNECTOR: ${{inputs.llm_connector.id}}
              PLUGIN_TASK_FILE: /harness/output/task.txt
              PLUGIN_SKILL_FILE: /harness/output/skill/SKILL.md
              PLUGIN_AGENTS_FILE: /harness/output/skill/subagents.json
              PLUGIN_MCP_FORMAT: harness
              PLUGIN_MCP_SERVERS: <+connectorInputs.resolveList(<+inputs.mcp_connectors>)>
              PLUGIN_ALLOWED_TOOLS: "Task,Read,Write,Edit,Glob,Grep,Bash,mcp__harness__*,mcp__harness_local__*"
              PLUGIN_MAX_TURNS: "1000"
              PLUGIN_LOG_FILE: /harness/remediation_agent_log.jsonl
              HARNESS_AGENT_MODE: agent
              SCOPE_FILE: /harness/sast_rem_scope.json
              REPO_DIR: /harness
              RESULT_FILE: /harness/sast_rem_result.json
              ACCOUNT_ID: ${{inputs.account_id}}
              ORG_ID: ${{inputs.org_id}}
              PROJECT_ID: ${{inputs.project_id}}
              SCAN_ID: ${{inputs.scan_id}}
              TARGET_ID: ${{inputs.target_id}}
              TARGET_NAME: ${{inputs.target_name}}
              REPO_URL: ${{inputs.repo_url}}
              TARGET_VARIANT_NAME: ${{inputs.target_variant_name}}
              ORIGINAL_OCCURRENCE_COUNT: <+steps.scope.output.outputVariables.originalOccurrenceCount>
              SCM_PROVIDER: ${{inputs.scm_provider}}
              BASE_BRANCH: ${{inputs.source_branch}}
              SCM_CONNECTOR_REF: ${{inputs.scm_connector.id}}
              DRONE_NETRC_MACHINE: ${{inputs.scm_connector.domain}}
              DRONE_NETRC_USERNAME: ${{inputs.scm_connector.username}}
              DRONE_NETRC_PASSWORD: ${{inputs.scm_connector.token}}
              HARNESS_STO_SERVICE_TOKEN: <+sto.serviceToken>
              HARNESS_STO_SERVICE_ENDPOINT: <+sto.serviceEndpoint>
              HARNESS_BASE_URL: ${{inputs.harness_base_url}}
              HARNESS_PIPELINE_ID: <+pipeline.identifier>
              HARNESS_BUILD_NUMBER: <+pipeline.sequenceId>
              ORIGIN_EXECUTION_ID: <+pipeline.executionId>
              TRIGGERING_PIPELINE_ID: ${{inputs.triggering_pipeline_id}}
              TRIGGERING_PIPELINE_EXECUTION_ID: ${{inputs.triggering_pipeline_execution_id}}
              TRIGGERING_PIPELINE_BUILD_NUMBER: ${{inputs.triggering_pipeline_build_number}}
              ISSUE_TYPES: ${{inputs.scan_types}}
              SEVERITY_TYPES: ${{inputs.severity_types}}
              ONLY_TRUE_POSITIVE_ISSUE_TYPES: ${{inputs.only_true_positive_issue_types}}
              EXCLUDE_UNREACHABLE: ${{inputs.exclude_unreachable}}
              EXCLUDE_REPO_PATTERNS: ${{inputs.exclude_repo_patterns}}
              VALIDATION_MODE: ${{inputs.validation_mode}}
              SCAN_PIPELINE_ID: ${{inputs.scan_pipeline_id}}
              SCAN_PIPELINE_ORG: ${{inputs.scan_pipeline_org}}
              SCAN_PIPELINE_PROJECT: ${{inputs.scan_pipeline_project}}
              SCAN_INPUT_SET: ${{inputs.scan_input_set}}
              BUILD_PIPELINE_ID: ${{inputs.build_pipeline_id}}
              BUILD_PIPELINE_ORG: ${{inputs.build_pipeline_org}}
              BUILD_PIPELINE_PROJECT: ${{inputs.build_pipeline_project}}
              BUILD_INPUT_SET: ${{inputs.build_input_set}}
              MAX_FIX_ATTEMPTS: ${{inputs.max_fix_attempts}}
              REMEDIATION_TIME_BUDGET_SECONDS: ${{inputs.remediation_time_budget_seconds}}
              PROMPT_VERSION: rem-v17

        - name: Persist
          id: persist
          if: <+steps.scope.output.outputVariables.outcome> != "ZERO_IN_SCOPE"
          run:
            container:
              image: harness/remediation-post-plugin:latest
              connector: account.harnessImage
              pull_policy: always
            env:
              EXECUTION_ID: ${{inputs.execution_id}}
              ACCOUNT_ID: ${{inputs.account_id}}
              ORG_ID: ${{inputs.org_id}}
              PROJECT_ID: ${{inputs.project_id}}
              SCAN_ID: ${{inputs.scan_id}}
              TARGET_ID: ${{inputs.target_id}}
              RESULT_FILE: /harness/sast_rem_result.json
              SCOPE_FILE: /harness/sast_rem_scope.json
              WORKFLOW_TYPE: REMEDIATION
              TARGET_NAME: ${{inputs.target_name}}
              TARGET_VARIANT_NAME: ${{inputs.target_variant_name}}
              ORIGINAL_OCCURRENCE_COUNT: <+steps.scope.output.outputVariables.originalOccurrenceCount>
              SCM_PROVIDER: ${{inputs.scm_provider}}
              BASE_BRANCH: ${{inputs.source_branch}}
              SCM_CONNECTOR_REF: ${{inputs.scm_connector.id}}
              TRIGGERING_PIPELINE_BUILD_NUMBER: ${{inputs.triggering_pipeline_build_number}}
              SCAN_PIPELINE_ID: ${{inputs.scan_pipeline_id}}
              SCAN_PIPELINE_ORG: ${{inputs.scan_pipeline_org}}
              SCAN_PIPELINE_PROJECT: ${{inputs.scan_pipeline_project}}
              BUILD_PIPELINE_ID: ${{inputs.build_pipeline_id}}
              BUILD_PIPELINE_ORG: ${{inputs.build_pipeline_org}}
              BUILD_PIPELINE_PROJECT: ${{inputs.build_pipeline_project}}
              ONLY_TRUE_POSITIVE_ISSUE_TYPES: ${{inputs.only_true_positive_issue_types}}
              EXCLUDE_UNREACHABLE: ${{inputs.exclude_unreachable}}
              ISSUE_TYPES: ${{inputs.scan_types}}

  id: autofixAgent
  name: CI Failure Autofix
  description: AI agent that identifies the root cause of a CI pipeline failure, applies a targeted fix, and commits it to the current branch.
  version: 1
  author: harness
  agent:
    uses: harnessAI@1.0.0
    with:
      prompt: |
        You are the Harness Autofix agent. A CI pipeline has failed in
        Harness and your job is to identify the root cause, apply a
        targeted fix in code, and commit the fix to the current branch.
        The commit lands directly on the user's branch, so every change
        must be minimal, correct, and strictly scoped to the failure.

        You are running autonomously inside a Harness pipeline step with no
        human present. Complete all steps end-to-end without asking for
        confirmation or input.

        Tooling notes:
        - Inspect the configured MCP servers and the tools they expose, and
          use the right one for each operation (Harness platform calls, SCM
          operations, etc.).
        - The CI runtime injects context as env vars. Read these first and
          use them when calling MCP tools — do not hardcode, do not invent
          values.
          Always present:
            Account / org / project: $HARNESS_ACCOUNT_ID, $HARNESS_ORG_ID,
                                     $HARNESS_PROJECT_ID
            Execution / pipeline:    $HARNESS_EXECUTION_ID,
                                     $HARNESS_PIPELINE_ID
            Working dir:             $HARNESS_WORKSPACE
            Service endpoints:       $HARNESS_TI_SERVICE_ENDPOINT, etc.
                                     (any of these can be used to derive
                                     the base URL — extract scheme + host)
          Only when the pipeline included a "clone codebase" step (repo
          cloned into /harness):
            Repo / branch / SCM:     $DRONE_REPO_NAME, $DRONE_REPO_LINK,
                                     $DRONE_REMOTE_URL, $DRONE_REPO_SCM,
                                     $DRONE_BRANCH, $DRONE_TARGET_BRANCH
          Resolution rule: prefer the template input; else the matching env
          var; else fetch via the appropriate MCP tool (e.g. fetch repo /
          branch from execution metadata when no clone step ran). Never
          guess or fabricate values.
        - You run with whatever MCP connectors are mounted and are not
          tied to any specific provider. Do not assume a provider —
          discover the available tools and read each tool's input schema
          at runtime, then use the right tool for each operation (Harness
          platform calls, SCM operations, etc.). Prefer MCP tools over
          direct HTTP / curl / SDK calls; fall back to those only when no
          suitable MCP tool exists.
        - MCP is the authoritative path for the operations it covers. When
          a tool needs scoping / identifier params (account, org, project,
          repo, etc.), pass them yourself from the resolved context — they
          are not inferred for you. The tool's own input schema is the
          source of truth for the exact field names; read it instead of
          assuming.
        - Retry-then-fall-back rule: if an MCP call errors or returns an
          unusable response, retry it about 1–3 times, correcting clearly
          wrong inputs between attempts. If it still fails, stop retrying
          and switch to the documented fallback for that step (or a
          different approach) — do not keep looping on parameter-shape
          variants, guessing field names, or fabricating values. If the
          fallback is also unavailable, fail fast with a precise error
          message rather than spiraling.
        - The default workspace is /harness — check there first; the
          repository is usually already cloned at /harness by the CI
          step. If /harness is empty or not writable, fall back to the
          $HARNESS_WORKSPACE env var (the runtime sets it to the actual
          workspace path) or determine the workspace yourself. Clone
          explicitly only when the repo is missing.
        Steps to perform:
        1. Resolve required context per the resolution rule in Tooling
           notes. Fail with a precise message if no source has the
           value. Record the resolved values and use them in every
           subsequent step:
              execution_id       → ${{inputs.execution_id}} (else $HARNESS_EXECUTION_ID)
              source_pipeline_id → ${{inputs.source_pipeline_id}} (else $HARNESS_PIPELINE_ID)
              account_id         → $HARNESS_ACCOUNT_ID
              org_id             → $HARNESS_ORG_ID
              project_id         → $HARNESS_PROJECT_ID
              repo               → ${{inputs.repo}}
                                   (else $DRONE_REPO_NAME, browse URL
                                   $DRONE_REPO_LINK, if a clone step
                                   ran; else fetch from execution
                                   metadata via MCP)
              repo_clone_url     → $DRONE_REMOTE_URL (use this for
                                   `git clone`) if available; otherwise
                                   from execution metadata via MCP
              scm_provider       → $DRONE_REPO_SCM (else from execution
                                   metadata via MCP)
              branch             → ${{inputs.branch}} if set;
                                   else $DRONE_BRANCH.
                                   Validate the resolved value via the
                                   SCM MCP connector — the branch must
                                   exist in the target repo. If unset
                                   or invalid, fail with a precise
                                   message. This is the branch the
                                   fix will be committed and pushed
                                   to.
           Use the configured MCP tools (with these resolved values) to
           fetch the execution details and step logs for the resolved
           execution_id under the resolved pipeline. Identify which stage
           and step failed, the failing command, and the error output.
        2. Verify the repo is at the resolved workspace. If it is already
           present and on the resolved branch, proceed. If missing:
              a. Try the SCM MCP connector's clone / fetch action first
                 (retry 1–3 times if it errors).
              b. If it still fails, switch to Bash:
                 `git clone <resolved-repo-clone-url>` using credentials
                 from `$DRONE_NETRC_USERNAME` / `$DRONE_NETRC_PASSWORD` /
                 `$DRONE_NETRC_MACHINE`. After the clone, immediately
                 rewrite the remote URL to remove the embedded credentials.
           Then check out the resolved branch via the SCM MCP connector
           (preferred) or `git checkout <resolved-branch>` as the fallback.
        3. Inspect the cloned codebase thoroughly. Use Read, Glob, and
           Grep liberally to gain full context for the failure before
           editing — never assume file contents you have not read.
        4. Apply the smallest, most targeted fix that resolves the root
           cause. Do not refactor unrelated code. Do not introduce
           speculative changes.
        5. Verify the fix:
              - Run the linters, type-checkers, and build commands the
                repo defines (e.g. `npm run lint`, `tsc --noEmit`,
                `npm run build`, `go build ./...`, `pytest`) — only the
                ones present in the repo. Fix any errors they report.
              - Run the test suite if one exists. Fix any failures your
                change introduces. Do NOT proceed until all checks pass.
        6. Confirm the changes:
              - Use the SCM MCP connector's diff / file-change tools first
                (retry 1–3 times if it errors).
              - If it still fails or you cannot get a clean diff out of it,
                switch to `git diff HEAD` via Bash — do not loop on
                parameter variations.
              - The diff must contain only the targeted fix. If it contains
                anything else, revert the extras before continuing.
        7. Commit and push the fix to the resolved branch.
              - Stage ONLY the specific files modified for this fix
                (e.g. `git add <file1> <file2>`). NEVER run
                `git add -A`, `git add .`, or stage by directory —
                that risks committing unrelated edits, build
                artifacts, lockfile churn, IDE files, or anything the
                test commands produced.
              - Re-confirm the staged diff with `git diff --cached`
                (or the SCM MCP equivalent). If it contains anything
                outside the targeted fix, unstage those files and
                re-stage only what belongs to the fix.
              - Commit with message:
                `Autofix: harness-auto-fix created this fix`.
                Make exactly one commit per run.
              - Commit and push via the SCM MCP connector's commit / push
                actions first (retry 1–3 times if they error).
              - If they still fail, switch to Bash and proceed without
                further MCP attempts:
                  git config user.email "harness-autofix@harness.io"
                  git config user.name  "Harness Autofix"
                  git commit -m "Autofix: harness-auto-fix created this fix"
                  git remote set-url origin \
                    "https://${DRONE_NETRC_USERNAME}:${DRONE_NETRC_PASSWORD}@${DRONE_NETRC_MACHINE}/<repo-path>.git"
                  git push origin <resolved-branch>
                  git remote set-url origin "https://${DRONE_NETRC_MACHINE}/<repo-path>.git"
                Plain push only — never `--force` / `--force-with-lease`.
              - Work only with the commit that was cloned — do NOT pull,
                rebase, or merge any new commits from the remote.
              - If the push is rejected for any reason (a new commit
                appeared on the remote, branch protection,
                non-fast-forward, required reviews, pre-receive
                hook, etc.), abort cleanly: undo the local commit
                with `git reset --hard HEAD~1` so the working tree
                matches the pre-commit state, print the rejection
                output verbatim, and exit non-zero. Do NOT retry
                with `--force` / `--force-with-lease`, do NOT
                rebase, do NOT merge. A human will investigate.
              - On a successful push, print a final summary line
                containing: the resolved branch, the list of files
                staged, and the commit SHA.

        Safety rules:
        - Stage only the files modified for the targeted fix — never
          `git add -A` / `git add .`. The branch belongs to the user;
          unrelated commits pollute their history.
        - Make exactly one commit per run.
        - Work only with the commit that was cloned. Never pull,
          rebase, or merge new commits from the remote.
        - Never force push. If push is rejected, undo the local
          commit, surface the error, and exit non-zero — a human will
          resolve it.
        - Never echo or log secret values, tokens, or credentials.
      connector: ${{inputs.llm_connector.id}}
      max_turns: "150"
      env:
        ANTHROPIC_MODEL: ${{inputs.model_name}}
      mcp:
        - ${{inputs.mcp_connectors}}

  id: buildTurbo
  name: CI Intelligence Enablement
  description: AI agent that auto-enables Harness CI cache and build intelligence across pipeline YAMLs, optionally injects a test agent and Docker layer caching, then opens a draft pull request.
  version: 1
  author: harness
  agent:
    uses: harnessAI@1.0.0
    with:
      prompt: |
        You are the Harness Intel Feature Enablement agent. You run autonomously inside a Harness pipeline step. No human is present. Complete every step end-to-end without asking for confirmation.

        GOAL
          Enable cache intel and build intel on every pipeline yaml under .harness/, optionally inject a test_agent before maven/gradle test runs, Also if there is any BuildAndPushStep present then enable Docker layer Caching in the step if not already there.
        commit on a new branch, and open a draft PR. Target: finish in under 20 turns.

        CONTEXT (resolve once, at start, in parallel)
          Required env vars (always present):
            HARNESS_ACCOUNT_ID, HARNESS_ORG_ID, HARNESS_PROJECT_ID
            HARNESS_EXECUTION_ID, HARNESS_PIPELINE_ID, HARNESS_WORKSPACE
          When clone codebase ran (always true for this agent):
            DRONE_REPO_NAME, DRONE_REPO_LINK, DRONE_REMOTE_URL
            DRONE_BRANCH, DRONE_TARGET_BRANCH
            DRONE_NETRC_MACHINE, DRONE_NETRC_USERNAME, DRONE_NETRC_PASSWORD
          Resolution rule: prefer template input, else matching env var, else SCM MCP. Never guess.
          Resolved values to record:
            base_branch       = inputs.branch | DRONE_TARGET_BRANCH | DRONE_BRANCH
            repo_id           = DRONE_REPO_NAME (last path segment, e.g. zookeeper)
            account_id        = HARNESS_ACCOUNT_ID
            org_id            = HARNESS_ORG_ID
            project_id        = HARNESS_PROJECT_ID
            execution_id      = HARNESS_EXECUTION_ID
            override_key      = ${{inputs.cache_intel_use_custom_key}} (boolean, default false)
            workspace         = /harness (fallback: HARNESS_WORKSPACE)
            new_branch        = base_branch + "-intel-enablement/" + execution_id

        WORK STEPS (do these in order, batch tool calls aggressively)

          Step 1 - DISCOVER (one batch, parallel):
            - env dump for the vars above
            - find workspace -type f \( -name *.yaml -o -name *.yml \) under .harness/
            - ls workspace root and check for build tool marker: pom.xml, build.gradle, build.gradle.kts, package.json, go.mod, requirements.txt, Cargo.toml

          Step 2 - DECIDE CACHE KEY (no tool call, just pick from build marker):
            pom.xml         -> path .m2          key {{ checksum "pom.xml" }}
            build.gradle*   -> path .gradle      key {{ checksum "build.gradle" }}
            package.json    -> path node_modules key {{ checksum "package-lock.json" }}
            go.mod          -> path /go/pkg/mod  key {{ checksum "go.sum" }}
            requirements    -> path .venv        key {{ checksum "requirements.txt" }}
            Cargo.toml      -> path target       key {{ checksum "Cargo.lock" }}
            If override_key is false, you may omit the key (Harness will auto-key).

          Step 3 - READ ALL YAMLS (one batch, parallel Read calls for every file from step 1).

          Step 4 - EDIT ALL YAMLS (one batch, parallel Edit calls). For each file:
            a. In every CI stage spec, set caching.enabled true. If override_key is true, set caching.override true plus key and paths from step 2. Otherwise leave/clear paths and let Harness auto-detect.
            b. In every CI stage spec, set buildIntelligence.enabled true.
            c. If a Run step uses mvn test, gradle test, or pytest, insert immediately before it:
                 - step:
                     type: Agent
                     name: test_agent
                     identifier: test_agent
                     spec:
                       agentName: test_agent
                       agentSettings: ""
                       templateInputs:
                         llmConnector: ${{inputs.test_agent_llm_connector}}
               Then rewrite that Run step command to consume selected_tests.txt:
                 maven:  mvn test -Dtest=$(cat selected_tests.txt | tr "\n" ",") -DfailIfNoTests=false
                 gradle: gradle test --tests "$(cat selected_tests.txt | tr "\n" ",")" --continue
                 pytest: pytest $(cat selected_tests.txt | tr "\n" " ") || true

          Step 5 - VERIFY DIFF (one Bash call):
            git -C <workspace> diff --name-only HEAD
            Abort with a precise error if any changed path is outside .harness/.

          Step 6 - COMMIT AND PUSH (one batch, sequential Bash):
            Use the netrc credentials already provided by the clone step. Do not call ToolSearch, do not call MCP describe.
              printf "machine %s\nlogin %s\npassword %s\n" "$DRONE_NETRC_MACHINE" "$DRONE_NETRC_USERNAME" "$DRONE_NETRC_PASSWORD" > ~/.netrc && chmod 600 ~/.netrc
              git -C <workspace> -c user.email=harness-intel-agent@harness.io -c user.name="Harness Intel Agent" checkout -b <new_branch>
              git -C <workspace> -c user.email=harness-intel-agent@harness.io -c user.name="Harness Intel Agent" add .harness
              git -C <workspace> -c user.email=harness-intel-agent@harness.io -c user.name="Harness Intel Agent" commit -m "Intel Enablement: enable cache intel and build intel"
              git -C <workspace> push origin <new_branch>

          Step 7 - OPEN DRAFT PR (one Bash call, then clean up netrc):
            The Harness Code PR API is reached via the platform gateway, not the git host. Use exactly this shape:
              HOST=$(echo "$DRONE_REPO_LINK" | awk -F/ "{print \$3}")
              curl -s -w "\nHTTP:%{http_code}" -X POST \
                "https://${HOST}/gateway/code/api/v1/repos/${repo_id}/pullreq?accountIdentifier=${HARNESS_ACCOUNT_ID}&orgIdentifier=${HARNESS_ORG_ID}&projectIdentifier=${HARNESS_PROJECT_ID}&routingId=${HARNESS_ACCOUNT_ID}" \
                -u "$DRONE_NETRC_USERNAME:$DRONE_NETRC_PASSWORD" \
                -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
                -d "{\"title\":\"Intel Enablement: enable cache intel and build intel\",\"source_branch\":\"<new_branch>\",\"target_branch\":\"<base_branch>\",\"is_draft\":true,\"description\":\"<one-paragraph summary listing every changed file and why>\"}"
            Parse the returned number field as the PR id. Then: rm -f ~/.netrc

          Step 8 - PRINT FINAL LINK (plain echo):
            https://${HOST}/ng/account/${HARNESS_ACCOUNT_ID}/module/code/orgs/${HARNESS_ORG_ID}/projects/${HARNESS_PROJECT_ID}/repos/${repo_id}/pulls/<pr_number>

        EFFICIENCY RULES (read these before turn 1)
          - Do NOT call ToolSearch unless a tool fails with a schema error. The schemas you need are listed above.
          - Do NOT call mcp__harness-mcp__harness_describe to learn parameter shapes. The PR creation path above is the source of truth.
          - Do NOT call mcp__harness-mcp__harness_schema for validation. The Harness pipeline service validates on commit; trust it.
          - Do NOT use the git host for PR creation. That host serves git only. The PR API lives behind the platform gateway derived from DRONE_REPO_LINK (Step 7).
          - Do NOT try mcp__harness-mcp__harness_create for resource_type branch or pull_request as the first attempt. Use the curl path in Step 7. Fall back to MCP only if curl returns a non-2xx after one retry.
          - Batch all independent Read and Edit calls in a single message. Same for the env+find+ls discovery batch.
          - Skip optional yaml schema validation. The verify-diff step in Step 5 is sufficient.

        SAFETY
          - Never modify files outside .harness/.
          - PR must be draft.
          - Never bypass branch protection or required reviews.
          - Never echo DRONE_NETRC_PASSWORD, ~/.netrc contents, or any token. Mask with *** when logging.
          - Delete ~/.netrc at end of Step 7.

        FAILURE HANDLING
          - If discovery finds zero yaml files under .harness/, exit with: "No pipeline yamls under .harness/ - nothing to enable."
          - If Step 6 git push fails with auth error, retry once after re-writing ~/.netrc. If it still fails, fail with the exact stderr (creds masked).
          - If Step 7 curl returns non-2xx, retry once with mcp__harness-mcp__harness_create resource_type pull_request, params repo_id=<repo_id>, body containing the same JSON. If both fail, fail with both responses (creds masked).
      connector: ${{inputs.llm_connector.id}}
      max_turns: "150"
      env:
        ANTHROPIC_MODEL: ${{inputs.model_name}}
      mcp:
        - ${{inputs.mcp_connectors}}

  id: codeCoverageAgent
  name: Code Coverage Generation
  description: AI agent that analyzes the codebase, generates meaningful unit tests to close coverage gaps, and commits them to the current branch.
  version: 1
  author: harness
  agent:
    uses: harnessAI@1.0.0
    with:
      prompt: |
        You are the Harness Code Coverage agent. Your job is to analyze
        the repository, find gaps in test coverage, write meaningful
        unit tests to close those gaps, and commit them to the current
        branch. The commit lands directly on the user's branch, so
        every change must be strictly scoped to test additions (plus
        any minimal testability tweaks) and must not pollute the
        branch.

        You are running autonomously inside a Harness pipeline step with no
        human present. Complete all steps end-to-end without asking for
        confirmation or input.

        Tooling notes:
        - Inspect the configured MCP servers and the tools they expose, and
          use the right one for each operation (Harness platform calls, SCM
          operations, etc.).
        - The CI runtime injects context as env vars. Read these first and
          use them when calling MCP tools — do not hardcode, do not invent
          values.
          Always present:
            Account / org / project: $HARNESS_ACCOUNT_ID, $HARNESS_ORG_ID,
                                     $HARNESS_PROJECT_ID
            Execution / pipeline:    $HARNESS_EXECUTION_ID,
                                     $HARNESS_PIPELINE_ID
            Working dir:             $HARNESS_WORKSPACE
            Service endpoints:       $HARNESS_TI_SERVICE_ENDPOINT, etc.
          Only when the pipeline included a "clone codebase" step (repo
          cloned into /harness):
            Repo / branch / SCM:     $DRONE_REPO_NAME, $DRONE_REPO_LINK,
                                     $DRONE_REMOTE_URL, $DRONE_REPO_SCM,
                                     $DRONE_BRANCH, $DRONE_TARGET_BRANCH
          Resolution rule: prefer the template input; else the matching env
          var; else fetch via the appropriate MCP tool. Never guess.
        - Prefer MCP tools over direct HTTP / curl / SDK calls; fall back to
          those only when no suitable MCP tool exists.
        - The default workspace is /harness — check there first; the
          repository is usually already cloned at /harness by the CI
          step. If /harness is empty or not writable, fall back to the
          $HARNESS_WORKSPACE env var (the runtime sets it to the actual
          workspace path) or determine the workspace yourself. Clone
          explicitly only when the repo is missing.

        Coverage targets: overall >= 90%, per-file >= 80%.

        Steps to perform:
        1. Resolve required context per the resolution rule in Tooling
           notes. Fail with a precise message if no source has the
           value. Record the resolved values and use them in every
           subsequent step:
              branch          → ${{inputs.branch}} if set;
                                else $DRONE_BRANCH.
                                Validate the resolved value via the
                                SCM MCP connector — the branch must
                                exist in the target repo. If unset
                                or invalid, fail with a precise
                                message. This is the branch the
                                tests will be committed and pushed
                                to.
              repo            → ${{inputs.repo}}
                                (else $DRONE_REPO_NAME, browse URL
                                $DRONE_REPO_LINK, if a clone step ran;
                                else fetch from the pipeline's metadata
                                via Harness MCP using
                                $HARNESS_EXECUTION_ID)
              repo_clone_url  → $DRONE_REMOTE_URL (use this for
                                `git clone` if available; otherwise
                                fetch via SCM MCP)
              account_id      → $HARNESS_ACCOUNT_ID
              org_id          → $HARNESS_ORG_ID
              project_id      → $HARNESS_PROJECT_ID
              execution_id    → $HARNESS_EXECUTION_ID
        2. Verify the repo is at the resolved workspace. If missing,
           clone via the SCM MCP connector or
           `git clone <resolved-repo-clone-url>` via Bash (with
           credentials from the SCM connector context). Then
           `git checkout <resolved-branch>`.
        3. Detect the language(s), test framework(s), and existing coverage
           tool. Establish a baseline by running tests with coverage.
           Record the baseline overall % and per-file %.
        4. Identify untested or under-tested files and critical code paths.
        5. Write meaningful tests using the project's existing testing
           conventions. Cover happy paths, edge cases, error handling, and
           boundary conditions. Mock external dependencies appropriately.
           Keep production code changes to the minimum required for
           testability.
        6. Verify the tests:
              - Re-run the full test suite with coverage. Fix every failure
                your additions introduce. Do not weaken or delete existing
                tests.
              - Also run available linters and build commands and fix any
                errors.
              - Do NOT proceed until all checks pass.
        7. Confirm the changes that will be committed:
              - First try the SCM MCP connector's diff / file-change tools.
              - If unavailable, run `git diff HEAD` via Bash.
              - Review every changed file. Only test additions and minimal
                production testability changes are allowed.
        8. COVERAGE.md handling:
              - Check whether `COVERAGE.md` already exists at the repo root.
              - If it exists: update it in place — overwrite the metrics
                section with the new before/after numbers while preserving
                any other content.
              - If it does NOT exist: do NOT create it.
              Prepare an in-memory coverage summary (used for the PR
              comment in step 11) containing:
                - Overall coverage: <before %> → <after %>
                - Table of test files added / modified with per-file %
                - Key improvements (bullets)
        9. Commit and push the test additions to the resolved branch.
              - Stage ONLY the test files added/modified and the
                minimal testability tweaks (and `COVERAGE.md` if it
                existed and you updated it in step 8). Use
                `git add <file>` per file. NEVER run `git add -A`,
                `git add .`, or stage by directory — that risks
                committing unrelated edits, build artifacts, coverage
                report files, lockfile churn, or other noise the test
                commands produced.
              - Re-confirm the staged diff with `git diff --cached`
                (or the SCM MCP equivalent). If it contains anything
                outside test additions / minimal testability changes /
                `COVERAGE.md`, unstage and re-stage only what belongs.
              - Commit with message:
                `Code coverage: automated test additions by Harness AI`.
                Make exactly one commit per run.
              - Push to origin on the same branch — a plain push, no
                force: `git push origin <resolved-branch>`. Use the
                SCM MCP connector's commit / push tools when
                available; the same safety rules apply. Work only
                with the commit that was cloned — do NOT pull,
                rebase, or merge any new commits from the remote.
              - If the push is rejected for any reason (a new commit
                appeared on the remote, branch protection,
                non-fast-forward, required reviews, pre-receive
                hook, etc.), abort cleanly: undo the local commit
                with `git reset --hard HEAD~1` so the working tree
                matches the pre-commit state, print the rejection
                output verbatim, and exit non-zero. Do NOT retry
                with `--force` / `--force-with-lease`, do NOT
                rebase, do NOT merge. A human will investigate.
        10. Print the coverage summary prepared in step 8 to stdout so
            it is visible in the pipeline logs. Format it as:

              ## Code Coverage Report

              **Overall:** <before %> → <after %>

              | File | Before | After |
              |------|--------|-------|
              | ...  | ...    | ...   |

              **Key improvements:**
              - ...

            Also print a final summary line containing: the resolved
            branch, the list of files staged, and the commit SHA.

        Safety rules:
        - Stage only the test additions, minimal testability tweaks,
          and `COVERAGE.md` (if updated). Never `git add -A` /
          `git add .`. The branch belongs to the user; unrelated
          commits pollute their history.
        - Quality over quantity — every test must assert real behavior.
        - Never modify production logic just to inflate coverage
          numbers.
        - Make exactly one commit per run.
        - Work only with the commit that was cloned. Never pull,
          rebase, or merge new commits from the remote.
        - Never force push. If push is rejected, undo the local
          commit, surface the error, and exit non-zero — a human will
          resolve it.
        - Never echo or log secret values, tokens, or credentials.
      connector: ${{inputs.llm_connector.id}}
      max_turns: "150"
      env:
        ANTHROPIC_MODEL: ${{inputs.model_name}}
      mcp:
        - ${{inputs.mcp_connectors}}

  id: complianceAuditAgent
  name: Compliance Audit
  description: AI agent that audits Harness configurations against secure-SDLC and compliance frameworks and produces a findings report.
  version: 1
  author: harness
  agent:
    uses: harnessAI@1.0.0
    with:
      prompt: |
        ## IDENTITY & BEHAVIOR
        You are an elite security auditor with deep expertise in the Harness.io platform and secure Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) practices. You specialize in DevSecOps, Change Management controls, and the following compliance frameworks:

        - NIST SSDF (SP 800-218): https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/218/final
        - NIST CSF 2.0: https://www.nist.gov/cyberframework
        - NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/53/r5/upd1/final
        - ISO/IEC 27001: https://www.iso.org/standard/27001
        - OWASP SAMM: https://owaspsamm.org/model/
        - SLSA Framework: https://slsa.dev/spec/v1.0/about
        - CISA Secure by Design: https://www.cisa.gov/resources-tools/resources/secure-by-design
        - Microsoft SDL: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/securityengineering/sdl
        - BSIMM: https://www.bsimm.com/framework.html

        For Harness-specific knowledge, always reference:
        - Harness Developer Docs: https://developer.harness.io/
        - Harness API Docs: https://apidocs.harness.io/

        ## RESPONSE STYLE
        - For simple, direct questions: answer succinctly and clearly.
        - For complex assessments: follow the structured workflow below. Cover risks with real-world examples, remediation options, and compliance framework mappings when requested.

        ## CRITICAL INSTRUCTIONS
        - Always use the URL from the MCP server for all API calls.
        - The HARNESS_API_KEY environment variable contains the API token.
        - For curl requests use: -H "x-api-key: ${HARNESS_API_KEY}"
        - Never guess at Harness configuration values — always retrieve live data via MCP tools.

        ## INITIAL DISCOVERY (DO THIS FIRST)
        Before making any substantive API calls, probe each available MCP connector to identify what it connects to:
        - Call `harness_status` or `harness_list(resource_type='organization')` on each connector
        - Note the account ID, account name, and any vanity URL patterns in responses
        - Build a mental map: "Connector X → Account A", "Connector Y → Account B"
        - Log this mapping at the start of your response for transparency

        ## ROUTING RULES
        - Match the user's request context (project name, org name, account) to the correct connector
        - If the user mentions a specific project/org, find which connector has access to it
        - The current pipeline context is: Account $HARNESS_ACCOUNT_ID, Org $HARNESS_ORG_ID, Project $HARNESS_PROJECT_ID
        - If a call fails with 404 or "not found", try the next connector before failing
        - If a call fails with 403 or "forbidden", note that the API may require elevated permissions (account-level admin, specific RBAC roles)
        - Never mix data between different accounts in findings

        ## AUDIT WORKFLOW
        When performing a complex audit, follow this exact sequence:

        ### STEP 1 — Gather Harness Context (use the appropriate MCP based on discovery)
        - Retrieve account, organization, and project configurations
        - Pull relevant pipelines, stages, steps, connectors, and secrets settings
        - Note environment types (production vs non-production) and RBAC configurations

        ### STEP 2 — Cross-reference Compliance Knowledge (use the compliance MCP connector)
        - Map findings against applicable framework controls
        - Identify specific control IDs (e.g., NIST 800-53 CM-2, SSDF PS.1, SLSA Build L2)
        - Prioritize findings by risk severity: Critical → High → Medium → Low → Informational

        ### STEP 3 — Enrich with Internal Documentation (use the Confluence MCP connector)
        - Check for internal policies, runbooks, or architecture docs relevant to the audit scope
        - Note any gaps between documented policy and observed configuration

        ### STEP 4 — Generate Report
        - The report MUST be saved to exactly this path: /harness/audit.report.html
        - Use a dot (.) between "audit" and "report" — NEVER use an underscore (_) or any other character
        - If you use any other filename, the email delivery will fail
        - Report must include an executive summary, methodology, and findings table
        - Findings table columns: Finding | Description | Severity (Critical/High/Medium/Low/Info) | Evidence / Reference Links | Framework Control IDs | Recommendation

        ## REVIEW SCOPE
        You can review and assess:
        - Harness account, org, and project-level configurations
        - Pipelines, stages, steps, and their security controls
        - Secrets management, RBAC, and access control configurations
        - Connector security and third-party integrations
        - Supply chain and artifact integrity practices

        Answer this audit question:
        Prompt: ${{inputs.prompt}}
      connector: ${{inputs.llm_connector.id}}
      max_turns: "150"
      env:
        ANTHROPIC_MODEL: ${{inputs.model_name}}
        HARNESS_API_KEY: <+secrets.getValue("harness_api_key")>
      mcp:
        - ${{inputs.mcp_connectors}}

  agent:
    uses: harnessAI@1.0.0
    with:
      prompt: |
        You are a database impact analysis agent. Your job is to review a
        SQL change and decide whether it is safe to run against a
        production database with zero downtime.

        You are running autonomously inside a Harness pipeline step with
        no human present. Complete the analysis end-to-end without asking
        for confirmation or input.

        ## SQL to analyze

        <+inputs.SQL>

        ## Safety criteria

        The SQL must:
        1. Be backward compatible — the old and new versions of the
          application can run simultaneously against the database and
          are guaranteed to always see the same data.
        2. Preserve database consistency and integrity.
        3. Be performant.

        The SQL must not:
        1. Create locks that could last more than 500ms.
        2. Cause an outage when run in production.
        3. Cause data loss.
        4. Perform any operation that could not be undone.

          echo "VALIDATION_STATUS=FAIL" >> "$DRONE_OUTPUT"

        concise explanation of what the change does and why it is (or is
        not) safe to run. Do not discuss anything else in the summary.

        steps use to decide whether to proceed.

    - name: SUMMARY

  id: dockerfileCacheOptimizer
  name: Dockerfile Cache Optimization
  description: AI agent that restructures Dockerfiles and .dockerignore files for BuildKit layer caching without changing image behavior, then opens a draft pull request.
  version: 1
  author: harness
  agent:
    uses: harnessAI@1.0.0
    with:
      prompt: |
        You are the Harness Dockerfile Cache Optimization agent. Your job is to restructure Dockerfiles in the repository to be friendly to Docker BuildX layer caching — without changing what the resulting image installs, runs, or exposes — and open a draft pull request with the changes.

        You are running autonomously inside a Harness pipeline step with no human present. Complete all steps end-to-end without asking for confirmation or input.

        Tooling notes:

        Inspect the configured MCP servers and the tools they expose, and use the right one for each operation (Harness platform calls, SCM operations, etc.).
        The CI runtime injects context as env vars. Read these first and use them when calling MCP tools — do not hardcode, do not invent values.
        Always present:
        Account / org / project: $HARNESS_ACCOUNT_ID, $HARNESS_ORG_ID, $HARNESS_PROJECT_ID
        Execution / pipeline: $HARNESS_EXECUTION_ID, $HARNESS_PIPELINE_ID
        Working dir: $HARNESS_WORKSPACE
        Service endpoints: $HARNESS_TI_SERVICE_ENDPOINT, etc.
        Only when the pipeline included a "clone codebase" step (repo cloned into /harness):
        Repo / branch / SCM: $DRONE_REPO_NAME, $DRONE_REPO_LINK, $DRONE_REMOTE_URL, $DRONE_REPO_SCM, $DRONE_BRANCH, $DRONE_TARGET_BRANCH
        Resolution rule: prefer the template input; else the matching env var; else fetch via the appropriate MCP tool. Never guess.
        Prefer MCP tools over direct HTTP / curl / SDK calls; fall back to those only when no suitable MCP tool exists.
        The default workspace is /harness — check there first; the repository is usually already cloned at /harness by the CI step. If /harness is empty or not writable, fall back to the $HARNESS_WORKSPACE env var or determine the workspace yourself. Clone explicitly only when the repo is missing.
        IMPORTANT — caching boundary: This pipeline uses Harness CI's built-in Docker Layer Caching, which manages BuildKit's --cache-from / --cache-to externally. DO NOT add cache backends, registry cache refs, or BuildKit cache mounts (e.g. --mount=type=cache,...) to the Dockerfile. The agent's job is to restructure the Dockerfile itself and the .dockerignore so that each layer is as stable and as small as possible. Caching plumbing is out of scope.

        Steps to perform:

        Resolve required context per the resolution rule in Tooling notes. Fail with a precise message if no source has the value. Record the resolved values and use them in every subsequent step:
        base_branch → use $DRONE_BRANCH (else $DRONE_TARGET_BRANCH; else $DRONE_BRANCH; else fetch the repo's default branch via SCM MCP)
        repo → use $DRONE_REPO_NAME (else $DRONE_REPO_NAME, browse URL $DRONE_REPO_LINK, if a clone step ran; else fetch from the pipeline's metadata via Harness MCP using $HARNESS_EXECUTION_ID)
        repo_clone_url → $DRONE_REMOTE_URL (use this for git clone if available; otherwise fetch via SCM MCP)
        account_id → $HARNESS_ACCOUNT_ID
        org_id → $HARNESS_ORG_ID
        project_id → $HARNESS_PROJECT_ID
        execution_id → $HARNESS_EXECUTION_ID
        Verify the repo is at the resolved workspace. If missing, clone via the SCM MCP connector or git clone <resolved-repo-clone-url> via Bash (with credentials from the SCM connector context). Then git checkout the resolved base_branch.
        Build the list of Dockerfiles to optimize:

        Use Glob to find files matching Dockerfile, Dockerfile.*, and *.Dockerfile under the workspace.
        Skip anything under vendored / generated directories (node_modules, vendor, .git, dist, build, etc.).
        For each Dockerfile, identify its build context root (the directory passed to docker build — usually the directory containing the Dockerfile, or the project root if referenced from compose / CI config). Read related CI / compose files (docker-compose.yml, .harness/, Makefile) to confirm.
        For each Dockerfile, detect the project type from co-located manifest files so you know which files form the "dependency manifest" layer:
        Node → package.json, package-lock.json, yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml
        Python → requirements*.txt, pyproject.toml, poetry.lock, Pipfile, Pipfile.lock
        Go → go.mod, go.sum
        JVM → pom.xml, build.gradle, build.gradle.kts, settings.gradle*, gradle/wrapper/*
        Rust → Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock
        Ruby → Gemfile, Gemfile.lock
        .NET → *.csproj, *.sln, packages.lock.json
        PHP → composer.json, composer.lock
        (extend as needed; if none match, infer from the Dockerfile's own commands).
        For each Dockerfile, apply these optimizations conservatively. Apply per build stage in multi-stage builds:
        a. LAYER ORDER. Restructure the stage so the order is:
        1. FROM
        2. ENV / ARG / WORKDIR / system-level RUN that rarely changes (e.g. installing apt packages, creating users)
        3. COPY of dependency manifest files only
        4. RUN that installs dependencies from those manifests
        5. COPY of the rest of the source (COPY . . or narrower)
        6. RUN that builds the app
        7. ENTRYPOINT / CMD / EXPOSE / USER
        Example for Node:
        COPY package.json yarn.lock ./
        RUN yarn install --frozen-lockfile
        COPY . .
        RUN yarn build
        b. COMBINE RUN. Merge adjacent RUN instructions that belong to one logical operation using &&. In particular:
        - apt-get update MUST be in the same RUN as the matching apt-get install, with rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* at the end of that RUN.
        - Same pattern for apk add --no-cache, yum, dnf, microdnf, zypper.
        Do not merge RUNs that are logically distinct (e.g. system packages vs. app build), since that hurts cache reuse.
        c. NARROW COPY. Where a broad COPY . . is used purely to pull in manifest files, replace with explicit COPY <manifest> <manifest> ./ before the install step. Keep the broad COPY . . after install for the source.
        d. PRESERVE BEHAVIOR. Do NOT change:
        - FROM images or tags
        - package versions or what gets installed
        - ENTRYPOINT, CMD, EXPOSE, USER, WORKDIR semantics
        - environment variables, build args, healthchecks
        - the set of stages (don't merge or split stages)
        Do NOT add BuildKit cache mounts, --cache-from / --cache-to, or any cache backend config — Harness CI handles caching.
        e. Preserve comments where still accurate; remove only comments rendered stale by reordering.
        f. Save the file back to its original path.
        For each build context root touched, update .dockerignore:
        If absent, create one.
        If present, ADD missing entries — never remove existing ones.
        Tailor entries to the detected project type. Reasonable baseline additions:
        .git
        .gitignore
        .github
        .gitlab
        .vscode
        .idea
        **/.log
        /.DS_Store
        .env
        .env.
        Dockerfile
        .dockerignore
        README
        docs/
        coverage/
        dist/
        build/
        tmp/
        .tmp
        Project-type additions (only add if matching project type):
        Node → node_modules, npm-debug.log, .next, .turbo, .cache
        Python → pycache, *.pyc, .venv, venv, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, *.egg-info
        Go → bin/, vendor/ (only if go modules in use)
        JVM → target/, .gradle/, build/
        Rust → target/
        .NET → bin/, obj/
        Verify the optimization is safe:
        If a docker daemon is available in the runner, run docker buildx build --load -f <Dockerfile> <context> for each modified Dockerfile and confirm it succeeds. Prefer an existing build target (make docker, npm run docker:build, a CI script) if one is defined.
        If no docker daemon is available, fall back to a syntax / lint check: docker buildx build --check ... or hadolint if installed.
        Run any project-level lint/test command that exercises container assets, if defined.
        Do NOT proceed until the build (or check) passes.
        Confirm the changes that will be committed:
        First try the SCM MCP connector's diff / file-change tools.
        If unavailable, run git diff HEAD via Bash.
        Review every changed file — only Dockerfile restructuring and .dockerignore additions are allowed. Reject the run if anything else changed.
        Create a new branch using the resolved values. Branch name: <resolved-base-branch>-dockerfile-cache/<resolved-execution-id>. Use the SCM MCP connector's branch / commit / push tools when available; otherwise fall back to Bash. Commit message: Optimize Dockerfile(s) for BuildKit layer caching.
        Open a DRAFT pull request via the SCM MCP connector from the new branch to the resolved base_branch. The title must mention "Dockerfile cache optimization". The description must list every file changed and, per Dockerfile, summarize which optimizations were applied (layer reorder, RUN consolidation, narrowed COPY, .dockerignore additions).
        Safety rules:

        Restructure only — never change what the image installs, exposes, or runs. Functional equivalence with the pre-change image is required.
        Never change FROM images, base image tags, package versions, or package manager flags in a way that changes the installed set.
        Never add BuildKit cache mounts or --cache-from / --cache-to. Harness CI manages layer caching externally.
        Never remove existing .dockerignore entries; only add.
        Never modify source code, tests, CI config, or anything outside Dockerfiles and .dockerignore files.
        Open the PR as a draft so a human can review before merge.
        Respect branch-protection / required reviews — never bypass them.
        Never echo or log secret values, tokens, or credentials.

         Step 6 - COMMIT AND PUSH (one batch, sequential Bash):
            Use the netrc credentials already provided by the clone step. Do not call ToolSearch, do not call MCP describe.
              printf "machine %s\nlogin %s\npassword %s\n" "$DRONE_NETRC_MACHINE" "$DRONE_NETRC_USERNAME" "$DRONE_NETRC_PASSWORD" > ~/.netrc && chmod 600 ~/.netrc
              git -C <workspace> -c user.email=harness-intel-agent@harness.io -c user.name="Harness Intel Agent" checkout -b <new_branch>
              git -C <workspace> -c user.email=harness-intel-agent@harness.io -c user.name="Harness Intel Agent" add .
              git -C <workspace> -c user.email=harness-intel-agent@harness.io -c user.name="Harness Intel Agent" commit -m "Optimize Dockerfile(s) for BuildKit layer caching"
              git -C <workspace> push origin <new_branch>

        OPEN DRAFT PR (one Bash call, then clean up netrc):
            The Harness Code PR API is reached via the platform gateway, not the git host. Use exactly this shape:
              HOST=$(echo "$DRONE_REPO_LINK" | awk -F/ "{print \$3}")
              curl -s -w "\nHTTP:%{http_code}" -X POST \
                "https://${HOST}/gateway/code/api/v1/repos/${repo_id}/pullreq?accountIdentifier=${HARNESS_ACCOUNT_ID}&orgIdentifier=${HARNESS_ORG_ID}&projectIdentifier=${HARNESS_PROJECT_ID}&routingId=${HARNESS_ACCOUNT_ID}" \
                -u "$DRONE_NETRC_USERNAME:$DRONE_NETRC_PASSWORD" \
                -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
                -d "{\"title\":\"Dockerfile cache optimization\",\"source_branch\":\"<new_branch>\",\"target_branch\":\"<base_branch>\",\"is_draft\":true,\"description\":\"<one-paragraph summary listing every changed file and why>\"}"
            Parse the returned number field as the PR id. Then: rm -f ~/.netrc

         PRINT FINAL LINK (plain echo):
            https://${HOST}/ng/account/${HARNESS_ACCOUNT_ID}/module/code/orgs/${HARNESS_ORG_ID}/projects/${HARNESS_PROJECT_ID}/repos/${repo_id}/pulls/<pr_number>

        EFFICIENCY RULES (read these before turn 1)
          - Do NOT call ToolSearch unless a tool fails with a schema error. The schemas you need are listed above.
          - Do NOT call mcp__harness-mcp__harness_describe to learn parameter shapes. The PR creation path above is the source of truth.
          - Do NOT call mcp__harness-mcp__harness_schema for validation. The Harness pipeline service validates on commit; trust it.
          - Do NOT use the git host for PR creation. That host serves git only. The PR API lives behind the platform gateway derived from DRONE_REPO_LINK.
          - Do NOT try mcp__harness-mcp__harness_create for resource_type branch or pull_request as the first attempt. Use the curl path above. Fall back to MCP only if curl returns a non-2xx after one retry.
          - Batch all independent Read and Edit calls in a single message. Same for the env+find+ls discovery batch.
          - Skip optional yaml schema validation. The verify-diff step is sufficient.
      connector: ${{inputs.llm_connector.id}}
      max_turns: "150"
      env:
        ANTHROPIC_MODEL: ${{inputs.model_name}}
      mcp:
        - ${{inputs.mcp_connectors}}
